answer_text:
# 🏥 Medi-Cal — What You Need to Know

**Medi-Cal** is California's Medicaid program, providing free or low-cost health coverage to eligible Californians. Here is a comprehensive overview of the program and its latest changes:

---

## 📋 What Medi-Cal Covers

Covered benefits include seeing your doctor and going to the hospital or getting emergency care. Medi-Cal members can fill their prescriptions, get mental health supports, and receive treatment for substance use. Other services covered include regular checkups, shots/vaccines, long-term care, non-emergency medical transportation, dental, and vision care.

---

## 🔑 Key Recent & Upcoming Changes

### 1. 💰 Asset Limit Reinstatement (January 1, 2026)
Effective January 1, 2026, the asset limit will be reinstated for non-MAGI Medi-Cal programs, back to 2022 levels — **$130,000 for an individual**, and **$65,000 for each additional household member**.

In July 2022, the state increased the asset limit (for a household of one, from $2,000 to $130,000), and then in January 2024, eliminated it entirely. That elimination is now ending.

Countable assets include cash, money in a bank account, second vehicles, or a home or land that the person does not live in. One home is exempt if the applicant lives in it. Second homes are counted. Assets not counted toward the limit include one vehicle or personal items such as televisions or other household items.

### 2. 🔍 30-Month Lookback Period Returns
Transfers made on or after **January 1, 2024 through December 31, 2025**, will **NOT** be included in the look-back period. In 2026, Medi-Cal will begin to consider transfer penalties for individuals who transfer assets on or after January 1, 2026, for the purposes of becoming eligible for Long-Term Care Medi-Cal.

### 3. 🧑‍💼 Work & Community Engagement Requirements (January 1, 2027)
Starting January 1, 2027, adults ages **19–64 without children under 13** must meet **work, volunteer, school, or training requirements** to keep Medi-Cal. Exemptions apply for pregnancy, disability, serious health conditions, and other circumstances.

### 4. 📅 More Frequent Renewals (January 1, 2027)
Effective January 1, 2027, adults ages 19–64 will need to renew Medi-Cal **every six months** instead of annually. Missing deadlines could result in loss of coverage.

### 5. 🌎 Immigration Status & Eligibility Changes
Beginning January 1, 2026, new Medi-Cal applications for adults (ages 19 and up) who are undocumented can only qualify for **Emergency Medi-Cal** or **pregnancy-related Medi-Cal**. However, if you already had Medi-Cal or applied before January 1, 2026, you are eligible to keep your full-scope coverage, provided you still meet all other eligibility requirements.

### 6. 💵 Cost Sharing (Starting October 1, 2028)
Beginning October 1, 2028, some adults on Medi-Cal will pay small **copayments** for certain services, capped at **5% of household income**, with no copays for emergency care, checkups, pregnancy, pediatric, mental health, or community clinic services.

---

## ✅ Tips to Stay Enrolled

- Keep your contact information up to date with Medi-Cal to avoid missing important notices. Watch your mail, phone, text messages, and email, as the county uses all of those ways to contact members.
- Respond to any letters from your local county Medi-Cal office and any reminders from your health plan or community groups.

---
